correctness.rationale: TARGET route: claim falsifies the universal conjunction by refuting the inversion conjunct on the admissible round metric F0, which logically decides the conjunction. Verified: F0 induced by S^2 is smooth, reversible, projective with closed projective-line geodesics; lift identifies I_{F0},I^*_{F0} with Funk F up to positive constants by SO(3)-transitivity of incidence. Funk-Hecke gives F|_{H_{2k}}=L*P_{2k}(0) with P_{2k}(0)=(-1)^k C(2k,k)/4^k !=0, hence injectivity; script re-ran OK (nonzero to k<2000, |P|sqrt(pi k)->1, 0.99979 at k=600). Averaging any hypothetical finite-order linear D to SO(3)-invariant \bar D of same order via Haar integration preserves order and descends (rotations commute with antipodal map). Helgason rank-one theorem gives \bar D=P(Delta); on H_{2k}, P(4k^2+2k)*C0*a_k^2=1 with a_k=C(2k,k)/4^k. Wallis bounds 1/(2sqrt(k))<=a_k<=1/sqrt(k+1) independently verified numerically and analytically; DRAFT upper-induction line swaps (k+1)/(k+2) but correct inequality holds since RHS-LHS=3k+2>0 and lower holds since (2k+1)^2-4k(k+1)=1>0, so Lemma 3 conclusion true. Then R(k)=1/(C0 a_k^2) grows at least linearly (diverges) and at most linearly (<=4k/C0), incompatible with deg R=2deg P>=2 unless constant, which also diverges. Hence no finite-order differential D with D N=Id exists. No vacuity or type error.
